Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

Figure 3 shows how resistors may be connected to a power source with two switches, $S_1$ and $S_2$.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_4_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 3: 6 V battery and switch S1 in series with a 10 ohm resistor, then two branches: 20 ohm in series with switch S2, and 20 ohm alone.

incertitudes: Question 4 (c) : le montage garde toujours la résistance de 10 ohms en série ; j'ai donné la résistance totale du montage dans chaque cas (30 ohms et 20 ohms) et rappelé la résistance de la seule partie parallèle (10 ohms).

questions.enonce_markdown: Name two types of circuit connections. *[2 marks]*
Explain how you can use the two switches to get each of the circuit connections named in (a) above. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The $10\,\Omega$ resistor is always in the circuit when $S_1$ is closed.

- **Series connection:** close $S_1$ and leave $S_2$ **open**. Current can only flow through the lower $20\,\Omega$ resistor, so the $10\,\Omega$ and the $20\,\Omega$ resistors are in series.
- **Parallel connection:** close **both** $S_1$ and $S_2$. The current divides between the two $20\,\Omega$ resistors, which are now in parallel with each other (this combination being in series with the $10\,\Omega$ resistor).

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the resistance for each of the circuit types. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Series** ($S_1$ closed, $S_2$ open): $R = 10 + 20 = 30\,\Omega$.

**Parallel** ($S_1$ and $S_2$ closed): the two $20\,\Omega$ resistors in parallel give $\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}$, so $R_p = 10\,\Omega$. Adding the $10\,\Omega$ resistor in series, the total resistance of the circuit is $R = 10 + 10 = 20\,\Omega$.

(Checking the current from the $6\,\mathrm{V}$ source: $I = 6/30 = 0.2\,\mathrm{A}$ in the series case and $I = 6/20 = 0.3\,\mathrm{A}$ in the parallel case.)

questions.enonce_markdown: State the circuit type which is more commonly used in house wiring and justify the choice with a reason. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The **parallel** connection is used in house wiring. Reason: each appliance receives the full mains voltage and can be switched on or off independently; if one appliance or lamp fails, the others keep working.
